conventions.convention: The model is spin zero on complex L²(R³), with inner product linear in the first argument, m>0, explicit ℏ>0, and free and interacting operators on W²,²(R³). Potentials are prescribed model assumptions; parameters are symbolic rather than measured inputs.

Spatial nondimensionalization uses y=x/L*, E*=ℏ²/(2mL*²), D*f(y)=L*^(3/2)f(L*y), and τ=tE*/ℏ. The resolvent-tail cutoff and spectral shift are dimensionless. Stationary formulas retain physical x, k and r with W_x=2mV/ℏ² in inverse-square-length units.

Ordinary wave operators are Ω±=s-lim as t→±∞ of exp(itH/ℏ)exp(-itHfree/ℏ), and S=Ω+*Ω−. Completeness means that each range equals both H_ac(H) and the orthogonal complement of the closed eigenvector span.

The incident shape has unit amplitude; the physical beam field is √n_inc times that shape, with n_inc>0 in m⁻³. Cross sections compare the scattered-component current with J_inc=n_incℏk/m, under equal-channel elastic flux assumptions. The density factor cancels; stationary fields are not normalized L² preparations.

For central bounded compactly supported potentials, the regular reduced radial solution has φ_l(r)/r^(l+1)→1; the outgoing solution has exp(i(kr−lπ/2)) normalization. W(φ,f)=φf′−φ′f, S_l=conjugate(W)/W, and δ_l is read modulo π.

The resonance parameters permit every real E_r and Γ>0, but physical k(E), phase shifts and cross sections are assigned only for E>0. Full-real-axis Lorentzian comparisons do not extend the physical energy domain.

The attractive Coulomb comparison uses κ>0 and the positive logarithmic Dollard phase with reference time t*=2mℓ*²/ℏ. Changing the reference time gives ΩD±′=ΩD±Q± and SD′=Q+*SDQ−; completeness is unchanged, but the scattering operator is not asserted unchanged.

Square-well big-O expansions take k→0+ at fixed depth and radius. Depth comparisons follow that limit; finite scattering length requires cos(γa)≠0, while γa=(n+1/2)π has a separate threshold-resonance calculation.

load_bearing.statement: Declares the spin-zero scattering model, its bounded compact-support and integrable resolvent-tail potential classes, the assigned energy operators on W²,², spatial and energy scaling, ordinary wave operators, scattering operator and completeness vocabulary; pure Coulomb is excluded.

Under the stated domain inclusion and self-adjointness hypotheses, H=cA and H0=cA0 for c=ℏ²/(2m)>0; E_H(cB)=E_A(B), physical and rescaled flows and wave limits correspond, and spectral types and eigenvectors are preserved.

For a real bounded compact-support potential and k>0, I+K_k is boundedly invertible; its constructed stationary solution is H²_loc and solves the equation distributionally, has a smooth amplitude and uniform O(r⁻²) far-field and derivative errors, and gives dσ/dΩ=|f_k|² with finite total cross section.

For the declared real bounded compactly supported central potential at k>0, the amplitude has the absolutely convergent L² Legendre expansion with coefficients (2l+1)(S_l−1)/(2ik), |S_l|=1, and σ=(4π/k²)Σ_l(2l+1)sin²δ_l.

If q=‖K_k‖<1, ‖u−e_inc‖₂≤q‖e_inc‖₂/(1−q) and the stated uniform amplitude bound holds. For real or complex η with |η|q<1, the scaled amplitude has the stated uniform quadratic coupling-error bound without requiring q<1 for the base potential.

For the declared integrable dimensionless resolvent-tail class, H is self-adjoint on W²,², both ordinary wave operators are isometries with ranges H_ac(H)=H_c(H), H_sc(H)=0, and S is unitary. Compactly supported L² local parts plus tails bounded by C(1+|x|/L*)^(−1−δ), δ>0, satisfy the class; pure Coulomb fails even the general tail integrability criterion.

seams_checked.note: Contextual prerequisite; the scattering page supplies its own controlled Born theorem and does not borrow WKB, variational or perturbative conclusions without their hypotheses.
The real-multiplier/free-operator supplier is used with d=3, the correct Fourier coefficient and exact Sobolev domain. Its bounded-potential conclusion is not extended to singular tails.
Free differential identification, central vocabulary and the attractive Coulomb energy operator retain their domains, positive parameters and physical exclusions.
Positive scaling is applied to an already self-adjoint operator with c>0 on the unchanged domain; no one-dimensional scattering result is substituted for three-dimensional scattering.
P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and P7 remain adopted assumptions. SI dimensions are preserved, and symbolic model parameters are not presented as measured values.
The s=0 specialization preserves the L² class space, position and momentum assignments and Born position law. Stationary beam shapes are explicitly distinguished from preparations.
Assigned sharp observables retain self-adjointness, declared units and PVM readings. Cross sections are flux ratios, not probabilities inferred directly from the spectral outcome law.
The autonomous flows use exp(−itH/ℏ) and exact operator domains. Comparison constructions do not assert driven evolution or an apparatus realization.
Preparation vocabulary retains normalized rays and density operators; generalized stationary fields are expressly outside that state assignment.

Cook, completeness, Fredholm, stationary, Born, partial-wave and Dollard supplier hypotheses and signs are preserved. Spatial and energy scaling are explicit; zero-energy uniformity and ordinary Coulomb limits are not imported.
Depths and energies use joules, radii metres, amplitudes metres and cross sections square metres. All examples retain symbolic parameters and conditional empirical status.
Examples calculate declared model readings without identifying them with detector outcomes, finite samples or measured probabilities.
The sphere-integration supplier contributes its Countable Choice hypothesis and σ(S²)=4π, giving the correct radial normalization in the well and Yukawa checks.
